title: PHP Web-Server Integration
learning_outcomes: Explain what php web-server integration contributes to a PHP application.
Apply at least one of these concepts in a small example: apache integration.
Check one edge case and explain how to diagnose unexpected behavior.

content.intro: Production reliability includes repeatable builds, correct runtime configuration, secret separation, compatible migrations, health checks, logging, monitoring, and a rollback strategy—not only uploading source files. In this lesson, focus on apache integration; then compare it with nginx with php-fpm. Use the example to predict a result before checking it, and record one case where the behavior may differ.
content.why_it_matters: You will use php web-server integration when building readable, testable PHP programs. Its practical value is knowing which rule applies, what result to expect, and how to handle failure or unexpected input.

common_mistakes.problem: Copying a pattern without understanding its inputs and output.
common_mistakes.why: Small environment or type differences can change behavior.
common_mistakes.fix: Trace one example by hand, name expected outputs, and consult version-matched official docs.

common_mistakes.problem: Ignoring empty, invalid, or boundary input.
common_mistakes.why: Real data rarely matches only the simplest example.
common_mistakes.fix: Add a deliberate edge-case check before relying on the result.

common_mistakes.problem: Making several changes at once while debugging.
common_mistakes.why: It becomes difficult to identify which change caused the behavior.
common_mistakes.fix: Reduce the issue to one small reproducible case, change one cause, and retest.
